videos.title: Live: SportsCenter
videos.description: The latest news, highlights and inside information from every corner of the sports world is presented each day on "SportsCenter," ESPN's first-ever program when the network debuted in September of 1979. The flagship series airs an evening edition and a brand new midnight show each weekday before the stage is cleared for a live "SportsCenter" morning block that emphasizes fast-paced, highlights-driven reports and what's new on social media platforms.

videos.title: Live: College GameDay
videos.description: Originating from the site of one of the day's best matchups, with a sea of fans cheering wildly in the background, host Rece Davis and analysts Lee Corso, Kirk Herbstreit and Desmond Howard talk college football for three hours, reporting on the top teams, games, players and storylines. David Pollack and Maria Taylor contribute reports, interviews and features. Davis replaced longtime host Chris Fowler in 2015.

videos.title: Live: College Football
videos.description: The Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets (3-7, 2-5 ACC) host the No. 11 Wake Forest Demon Deacons (9-1, 6-1) in Atlanta. With only one loss this season, Wake Forest enters after beating SMU 49-7, while Georgia Tech beat Clemson 20-6 behind Alberto Mendoza.

videos.title: Live: College Football
videos.description: The No. 5 Texas Longhorns (8-2, 5-2 SEC) host the Arkansas Razorbacks (4-6, 2-5) in Austin. Arkansas enters after a 34-6 victory over South Carolina, while Texas seeks a fifth straight victory behind Arch Manning, who leads with 19 touchdowns.

videos.title: Live: College Football
videos.description: The No. 7 Miami Hurricanes (9-1) host the Virginia Tech Hokies (6-4) for an NCAA football game at Hard Rock Stadium. Virginia Tech aims to break a two-game skid behind Ethan Grunkemeyer, while Miami enters after a 36-25 win against Duke.

videos.title: Live: Sunday NFL Countdown
videos.description: This Sunday pregame staple debuted in 1985 and soon became a signature ESPN series. Host Mike Greenberg introduces the features and directs the storylines associated with the day's games, joined by a roster of analysts highlighted by ex-NFL players, coaches and executives including Tedy Bruschi, Randy Moss, Alex Smith, and Rex Ryan. Adam Schefter deliver breaking news and injury updates, while reporters at game sites set the scenes.

videos.title: Live: SportsCenter With Scott Van Pelt
videos.description: SVP's up at midnight and bringing his unique perspective on games people play to "SportsCenter" viewers. The hourlong, late-night show is driven by the host's self-deprecating wit and passion for sports, with featured elements, including Van Pelt's nightly "1 Big Thing" commentary and a weekly look back at the moments that drove bettors wild in "Bad Beats." The show also delivers what "SportsCenter" fans are used to -- news and highlights, guests and interviews -- but in a different, fast-paced and insightful way.

videos.title: Live: Get Up
videos.description: ESPN's morning show features host Mike Greenberg with a rotating and diverse group of analysts opining about and analyzing the latest news from the world of sports. The two-hour, personality-driven show originates from Hudson Square in Lower Manhattan, a modern media hub for ESPN and The Walt Disney Company's New York-based teams. Greenberg, aka "Greeny," is formerly one-half of ESPN Radio's longtime "Mike & Mike" morning show.

videos.title: Live: First Take
videos.description: Stephen A. Smith hosts this weekday morning sports debate show. Smith provides his expert takes on the day's trending sports topics and under-the-radar news. They're regularly joined by veteran analysts and the top guests in sports and entertainment.

videos.title: Live: The Pat McAfee Show
videos.description: Pat McAfee brings his humor and candor; he and his cast of characters unpack the day's top stories and interview the biggest names in sports.

videos.title: Live: Big Day With Peter Schrager
videos.description: Peter Schrager's daily show will feature rotating panelists focusing heavily on the NFL while also providing coverage of other major sports stories.

videos.title: NFL Live
videos.description: Host Laura Rutledge takes the helm of this weekday show featuring the likes of Marcus Spears, Dan Orlovsky, Mina Kimes, and Adam Schefter. The "NFL Live" crew entertains fans while offering all the latest news and analysis from across the NFL.

videos.title: Live: Pardon the Interruption
videos.description: The debate is the story in this fast-paced, half-hour series hosted by former Washington Post sportswriters Tony Kornheiser and Michael Wilbon. The pair engage in high-energy discussions, conduct interviews and often argue over topics not even related to sports. Other sports reporters appear as guests and offer opinions on the top stories of the day.

videos.title: Live: Monday Night Countdown
videos.description: Previewing the Monday Night Football matchup airing later on ESPN. Host Scott Van Pelt is joined by Ryan Clark, Jason Kelce, Marcus Spears, Adam Schefter and Michelle Beisner-Buck as they analyze every last morsel of information pertaining to Monday night's combatants, plus discuss the latest news that developed out of Sunday's action.

videos.title: Live: Monday Night Kickoff
videos.description: The legendary Monday Night Football crew of Joe Buck, Troy Aikman, and Lisa Salters preview the upcoming Monday Night Football action.

videos.title: Live: NFL Football
videos.description: The Washington Commanders host the Cincinnati Bengals in NFL regular-season play at Northwest Stadium. Cincinnati arrives at 7-2 and winner of five straight, while Washington sits at 3-5-1 after alternating wins and losses over its last four games.

videos.title: Live: Monday Night Postgame
videos.description: A recap of the Monday Night Football matchup with highlights, interviews and more.
